bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/synchronization.rs (bifrost_app::synchronization: Mutex with with_lock and with_lock_if_available, Atomic over six fixed-width integers, AtomicLazyReference, LoadOrdering/StoreOrdering/UpdateOrdering, atomic_memory_fence); std::sync primitives remain available to apps directly
summary: Apple's framework is a set of low-level primitives: typed atomics, a lazy atomic reference, a closure-scoped Mutex, memory-ordering enums and an atomic fence. BifrOSt now provides an SDK module that mirrors the Mutex, the ordering enums, the fence, the integer Atomic operations and AtomicLazyReference on std only. WordPair is still missing: a lock-free double-word atomic needs unsafe code or a platform instruction, which the pure-Rust rule rules out. Custom AtomicRepresentable types are not provided.

features.apple: Atomic<Value> with add, bitwiseAnd, load, store, exchange, compareExchange (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/atomic)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/synchronization.rs (Atomic<T>, AtomicInteger); springboard/sdk/src/dispatch.rs:108 (AtomicU64 in the pool)
features.note: Atomic<T> over u32, u64, usize, i32, i64 and isize with load, store, exchange, compare_exchange, compare_exchange_with, add, subtract, bitwise_and, bitwise_or and bitwise_xor, each returning (old, new) as the framework does. Missing: AtomicRepresentable custom types, Bool and Optional atomics, and Apple's exact generic constraint

Implemented with std OnceLock over Arc<T>: load returns None while nil and store_if_nil keeps the first value. Holds Arc<T>, not an AnyObject reference, so there is no Objective-C-style object or unowned reference

features.apple: WordPair, a pair of two word-sized UInts stored atomically (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/wordpair)
features.note: Not built: a lock-free double-word compare-and-exchange needs unsafe code or a platform instruction (cmpxchg16b); the pure std rule for this framework rules it out. A Mutex-backed pair would not be atomic in the same sense and is not offered
Swift protocol mechanism for storing custom types atomically; Rust uses the fixed std atomic types, so there is no counterpart to expose

Case sets match the framework: relaxed, acquiring, sequentiallyConsistent (load); relaxed, releasing, sequentiallyConsistent (store); plus acquiringAndReleasing for updates. Each maps onto the std Ordering
Takes UpdateOrdering. A relaxed fence is a no-op because std rejects a relaxed fence; the other orderings call std::sync::atomic::fence

features.apple: Mutex<Value> with init, withLock and withLockIfAvailable (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/synchronization/mutex)
features.note: Closure-scoped with_lock and with_lock_if_available (returns Option, never blocks). A poisoned lock is recovered, as the SDK does elsewhere

gaps: No WordPair or double-word atomic: a lock-free pair needs unsafe code or a platform instruction, which the pure std rule excludes
No AtomicRepresentable or AtomicOptionalRepresentable: Atomic covers the six fixed-width integer types only, not Bool, Optional or custom types
AtomicLazyReference holds Arc<T>; there is no object-reference equivalent beyond Arc
